gaps.text: In-line measurement of Process temperature with bioreactor temperature probe

Combining several spectroscopy methods (data fusion) (Low-level fusion: UV-Vis turbidity and fluorescence spectra from the same sampling spot, synchronised to a common time step, with one calibration block per method before any joined model. A combined or co-located probe arrangement is needed because separate alternating probes cannot guarantee the same measurement point. The fused model must beat the best single-method model on held-out runs, otherwise the fluorescence channel should be dropped.)

items.finding: Multimodal fusion technology demonstrates value in spectral analysis by combining inputs, but the effectiveness of sensor fusion does not increase proportionally with the number of sensors and relies on complementarity.
items.how_it_applies: When combining UV-Vis and fluorescence data streams, evaluate whether the added channel provides independent information rather than just increasing system complexity.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The cited findings relate to egg and food quality evaluation rather than mammalian cell bioreactors, so fusion performance and sensor complementarity must be validated on actual bioprocess data.

citation.quote: It is noteworthy that the effectiveness of multi-sensor fusion does not increase proportionally with the number of sensors; rather, it hinges on mutual correction and complementarity among different sensors.
citation.label: E05 ¶29

items.finding: Before fusing data from multiple sources, evaluating the contribution and complementarity of each dataset is essential.
items.how_it_applies: Perform individual model evaluations for the UV-Vis and fluorescence channels before constructing the joint low-level fusion model.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The reference discusses general PAT data fusion and specific analytical studies, meaning specific feature contributions may differ in a stirred mammalian cell bioreactor.

citation.quote: Before fusing data from multiple sources, it is essential to evaluate the contribution of each dataset to the model and its complementarity.
